text:
sam: heads-up — we got a control-plane spike in us-west1 around 10:02 UTC after the GPU pool scaled in. apiserver returned lots of 502/503s and controller-manager liveness started flapping. etcd leader CPU jumped to ~95% and watch queue depth exploded. anyone digging?

anya: saw the alerts. apiserver on control-plane-3 hit ~1.9Gi RSS then OOM-killed some listener threads. logs show repeated `watchQueueDepth` growth and `watchCache: tombstone` churn. looks like a fanout storm when many node leases expired.

matt: pasted small log excerpt:
```
I0318 10:02:15.123 apiserver.go:345] watchQueueDepth: resource=pods queue=4812
E0318 10:02:16.004 controller-runtime: reconciler error: timeout getting pod list: Get \"/api/v1/pods?watch=true\": 502
I0318 10:02:18.450 etcdserver: read-only range request too slow, applied index lagging
```

priya: GPU autoscaler for that pool ran a fast scale-in yesterday — config has `scaleInCooldown: 30s` to save cost. when 150 GPU nodes went NotReady -> terminated, controller-manager & apiserver had to push huge number of watch events (leases, endpoints, evictions). cost tradeoff bite back. :grimacing:

srebot: incident created: INC-2026-1768 (control-plane-watch-fanout-us-west1). SLO impact detected: apiserver 99th p99 latency increased, error budget burn in region.

sam: initial triage: probable root chain: aggressive gpu-scalein -> mass lease/node eviction -> huge watch fanout -> kvcache misses / apiserver threads blocked -> etcd leader CPU + io spike -> apiserver 5xxs -> controller-manager misses heartbeat -> liveness restarts. Need quick mitigations and longer-term fixes.

matt: quick mitigation ideas (short-term):
- throttle the autoscaler scale-in in us-west1 (raise cooldown to 600s)
- patch controller-manager to increase livenessProbe timeout by 2x as a buffer
- increase apiserver watch cache memory limit on control-plane-3 or redistribute leader affinity

priya: agree. I'll patch the autoscaler cooldown first. Command I'm about to run: 
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap/gpu-autoscaler --type merge -p '{"data":{"scaleInCooldown":"600s"}}'
```
Doing a canary in us-west1-only.

anya: i'll also kick a controlled restart of control-plane-3 after the autoscaler patch lands to clear stuck watchers. Will schedule in ~2m and watch etcd CPU.

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted: patch/gpu-autoscaler (canary: us-west1) by priya. CI checks passed.

sam: after the canary, let's monitor watchQueueDepth and etcd leader CPU. long-term we should:
- add burst-protection to the autoscaler (max parallel terminations)
- surface a watch-fanout metric into Redwood Console and auto-throttle scale-ins when watchQueueDepth > X
- consider moving lease eviction smoothing into kubelet/leases (batch lease expirations)
- evaluate moving control-plane-3 leader placement away from noisy IO hosts

matt: also toss in a short-term etcd tweak: increase `--max-wal-fsync-duration`? (only if IO is spiky) or add an additional etcd follower with higher IO in that AZ.

priya: can confirm autoscaler cooldown patch applied (us-west1 canary). watching now.

anya: control-plane-3 restart complete, watchers re-established. early signs: watchQueueDepth down to ~300, etcd leader CPU dropping to ~55%. apiserver 5xxs reduced.

sam: great — keep monitoring for 30m. follow-ups: file a task to update autoscaler heuristics, add test harness for simulated mass-node-termination, and add playbook steps for future similar incidents. thanks team :thumbsup:

srebot: incident INC-2026-1768 updated: mitigated -> monitoring.
